en: Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*) and of resultant nature (*vipāka*), a state that is not-conflict and not of resultant nature arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). [Under] root [condition], there is one; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance [condition], there is one.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and of a nature to produce resultants (*vipākadhammadhamma*), a state that is not-conflict and not of a nature to produce resultants arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict and of a nature to produce resultants, a state that is not-conflict and not of a nature to produce resultants arises by way of root condition.
Under the root condition, there are two; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, there are two.

Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) and neither-result-nor-state-leading-to-result, there arises a state that is without refuge (*nasaraṇa*) and neither-result-nor-state-leading-to-result by way of the root condition. Under the root condition, there is one; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, there is one.
